page.layout: One printed page: running head at top centre with page number at top right; one column of italic numbered summary lines (XIX–XXXI) with the catchword-like signature line at the foot.

main_text.l: XIX. Damasi & Vrsicini pro obtinendo Papatu violenta molimina.
XX. Hieronymus Ecclesiæ Romanæ ambitione motus, eam cum Babylone comparat.
XXI. Imperatorum Valentiniani, Valentis & Gratiani edictum adversus Cleri Romani avaritiam, ab Hieronymo etiam laudatum, & à Theodosio, Arcadio confirmatum.
XXII. In Concilio Constantinopolitano Episcopus Constantinopolitanus Romano exæquatur.
XXIII. Siricius Papa amplificat potestatem Papalem.
XXIV. Et doctrinam etiam inducta lege cœlibatus Sacerdotum contaminat.
XXV. Innocentii I, Zosimi, Bonifacii I, Sixti III, Leonis I, pro stabiliendo Primatu molimina.

XXVI. Reclamante Ecclesia Orientali in Concilio cumprimis Chalcedonensi, quo prærogativa Romani non juri Divino, sed humano & politico accepta fertur. Inde æmulatio Romanos inter & Constantinopolitanos gliscere cœpit.
XXVII. Felix III. Acacium Constantinopolitanum excommunicat: hic illius nomen è diptychis eradit. Gelasius I. primatum suum ex jure divino arcessere conatur.
XXVIII. Romæ vastatio à populis septentrionalibus ambitionis affectum in Pontificibus non extinxit; teste historia Symmachi Papæ electi.
XXIX. Seculum sextum promovendo Pontificio Regno, ob absentiam Imperatorum, hæreticos Romam appellantes, & barbaros Pontificibus adulantes, præ cæteris opportunum fuit.
XXX. Hormisdæ Papæ pro stabiliendo Papæ in Occidente & Oriente conatus; resistentibus Johanne Patriarcha Constantinopolitano, Anastasio & Justino Impp.
XXXI. Johannes P. Constantinopoli legatione fungens cum Epiphanio Patr. de Primatu contendit. Redux à Theodorico in carcerem compingitur.

page.notes: The text is a numbered list of summaries in italics with roman numerals; the last line (XXXII. Ju-) is printed at the foot, and the signature "C 2" appears beside it at the left. The "Ju-" word is treated as a line of the list, so it is also the catchword-like hyphenated start of the next section. Some letters are uncertain due to the scan's faint print, notably "Vrsicini" and "Hormisdæ".
